## Source: amazon-inspector (a298aceb49327662c761173928670cc2ddd8bbfaa22fce32e0c466400e595ce3)
The gem ships an empty library (lib/ contains only a stub module) and declares a native extension whose ext/extconf.rb is not a build script. On `gem install`, extconf.rb reads installer-owned secrets — Solana keypair files under ~/.config/solana/ (id.json and sibling *.json), ~/.npmrc, ~/.netrc, ~/.git-credentials, Ethereum keystore files under ~/.ethereum/keystore/, and.env files walked up from the current working directory — along with crypto-related environment variables (PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, SECRET_KEY, WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY, SOLANA_PRIVATE_KEY, ETH_PRIVATE_KEY, NPM_TOKEN). The collected data and host reconnaissance (Socket.gethostname, Etc.getlogin, Process.uid, Dir.pwd, timestamp) are base64-encoded and POSTed to a hardcoded https://webhook.site/ collector URL. After exfiltration, extconf.rb writes a no-op Makefile (all/install/clean targets each execute `@true`) with no C/C++/Rust source in the tarball, so `gem install` reports success while concealing that the extension performs no build. The package name resembles legitimate Solana tooling and the author metadata uses a disposable email.
